expected: The team met this morning to go over the plan for the next release. Most of the work on the new settings screen is finished and tested. We still need to decide how the export button should behave on small windows. The designers want a single menu while the engineers prefer two separate buttons. We agreed to try the single menu first and see what people say. The second topic was the backlog of support requests from last month. Many of those requests ask for a way to undo a deleted note. An undo button would cover most of them without any new settings. The support lead will sort the rest of the requests by how often they come up. After that we talked about the slow start on older laptops. The profile showed that loading every note at launch takes most of the time. Loading only the recent notes first should make the window appear much sooner. The older notes can then load quietly in the background. We also need better tests for the sync code before we change it. The current tests only cover the happy path and miss most of the failures. Each engineer will write tests for the part of the sync code they know best. The release date stays the same unless the tests turn up something serious. Marketing asked for a short video that shows the new settings screen. The video should be ready a week before the release goes out. The documentation team will update the help pages at the same time. There was a short discussion about moving the weekly meeting to the afternoon. Most people would rather keep it in the morning so nothing changes for now. The next meeting will review the test results and the support list. Please send any questions to the team channel before the end of the week. Thanks everyone for the careful work on this release so far. The last item was the budget for new test devices. We can buy two older laptops and one small tablet this quarter. The finance team will confirm the numbers by the end of the month. Until then we will borrow devices from the support team. That covers everything we planned to discuss today.

expected: Hello everyone. I wanted to give you a full update on the move to the new office before the end of the month. The lease for the new building was signed last week and the keys arrive on Monday. The removal company will pack the shared rooms first and leave the desks until the very last day. Each of you should pack your own desk on the Thursday before the move. Boxes and labels will be in the kitchen from Wednesday morning. Please write your name and your new room on every box you pack. Anything without a label will go into the storage room and may take a while to find. The network team will move the printers and the phones over the weekend. They expect everything to work by Monday morning, but they asked for some patience on the first day. If your laptop cannot reach the network in the new building, call the help desk rather than trying to fix it yourself. Parking at the new building is limited, so please use the train or the bus where you can. The station is a short walk from the front door and there is a covered path most of the way. We will hand out the new access cards at reception on Monday. Bring your old card with you so the security team can switch it off. The kitchen on the second floor will not be ready until the following week. Until then there is a small kitchen next to the meeting rooms on the ground floor. The cleaners will take away anything left in the old office after Friday, so please check your drawers twice. Old paper files should go into the locked bins rather than the normal recycling. If you have questions about the move, send them to the office manager by Wednesday. She will collect them and answer the common ones in a short note to everyone. Thank you all for your help with this, and I look forward to seeing you in the new space. Kind regards from the whole facilities team.

expected: Notes from the planning meeting on Tuesday. The meeting started a little late because the room was still booked by another team. We began with the budget for the next quarter, which is lower than we hoped. Travel will be cut back, and most visits to customers will happen over video instead. The hiring plan stays the same, with two engineers and one designer joining before the summer. The designer will work on the mobile app first and then move to the website. Next we looked at the support numbers from last month. The number of requests went down for the third month in a row. Most of the remaining requests are about passwords and billing, and both should get easier with the new settings page. The support lead asked for a clearer way to tag requests so the reports are easier to read. We agreed to try a short list of tags for one month and then review it. After that we talked about the release schedule. The next release is planned for the end of the month, and the one after that six weeks later. The team wants to ship smaller releases more often, but the testing still takes too long. Two people will spend the next sprint making the slow tests faster. If that works, we will move to a release every three weeks from the autumn. Then there was a long discussion about the data export feature. Customers keep asking for it, but the first version was harder to build than expected. We decided to ship a simple export that covers the common cases and leave the rest for later. The product manager will write a short note explaining what the first version does and does not do. Finally we looked at the office plants, which nobody has watered for a fortnight. A volunteer offered to take care of them on Mondays and Thursdays. The next planning meeting is in four weeks, and the agenda will go out a few days before.
